description: Rootkit Hunter scan reported 1 suspect file and configuration warnings: a root-equivalent test account and a passwordless account were found

warnings: Found passwordless account in shadow file: test1
The file of stored file properties (rkhunter.dat) does not exist

recommendation: Review the flagged account(s) for legitimacy, remove root-equivalent UID=0 accounts other than root, set a password on any passwordless account, and run 'rkhunter --propupd' after confirming the system is clean to refresh the baseline.

description: Rootkit Hunter scan found suspicious file types in /dev and a replaced system command (egrep swapped for a shell script)

warnings: Suspicious file types found in /dev: /dev/shm/ad_connect_queue evt_event_mtx: data
The command '/usr/bin/egrep' has been replaced by a script

recommendation: Inspect the flagged /dev entries for legitimacy, verify replaced system commands against package-manager-provided originals, and re-run a full scan after remediation to confirm the findings clear.

description: authorized_keys grew from 1 to 2 keys for user root — possible SSH key injection
recommendation: Immediately review the new key in authorized_keys for that user, remove any key that wasn't added through an authorized process, rotate SSH credentials for the affected account, and audit recent SSH logins from unfamiliar source IPs.

description: A new file appeared inside a user's .ssh/ directory that was not present in the last baseline scan — possible backdoor
recommendation: Inspect the newly created file's contents for unexpected ProxyCommand/IdentityFile directives or additional trust anchors, remove it if unauthorized, and confirm the .ssh directory permissions remain 0700.

description: 3 new outbound connections detected to IPs/ports not seen during the 14-day learning baseline
recommendation: Investigate the new binary and destination for legitimacy; if unauthorized, terminate the process, block the destination IP/port, and inspect for persistence mechanisms. If legitimate (e.g. a new approved service), add it to the XML whitelist to prevent repeat alerts.

description: A new listening port was detected that was not present during the learning phase, bound to a binary not in the learned whitelist
recommendation: Treat an unrecognized listening service as high-priority — identify the process, terminate it if unauthorized, remove the binary, and check for the corresponding startup mechanism (cron, systemd, init script).

description: Both decoy honeypot processes (backupAgent, securityAgent) were found not running, and file-comparison checks against the reference backup reported corruption
recommendation: Treat as a high-priority ransomware indicator: isolate the host from the network immediately, verify backup integrity from an offline copy, restart the decoy processes only after confirming no active encryption is in progress, and preserve forensic evidence before remediation.

description: One of two decoy honeypot processes stopped running within the 24-hour observation window following a fresh install
recommendation: Confirm whether the decoy process stopped due to a legitimate service restart/update or an unauthorized termination; restart it and monitor closely, escalating if the second decoy also goes down.

description: 2 binaries under /usr/bin and /athinio/bin were modified within the last 24 hours, outside of any known update window
recommendation: Compare modified binaries against known-good hashes or package manager records, check for unauthorized package installs or manual edits, and restore from a trusted backup if tampering is confirmed.

description: The last-modified timestamp of /athinio/bin advanced outside the expected maintenance window, and driver counts under the running kernel module directory changed
recommendation: Identify what was added to /athinio/bin and cross-check against the deployment/change log; investigate the two new kernel driver entries for legitimacy before accepting the new baseline.

description: A monitored log file shrank by 12KB compared to its baseline size — possible log wiping to cover tracks
recommendation: Treat log truncation as a strong intrusion indicator: preserve remaining log content immediately, check for a corresponding gap in centralized/forwarded logs if available, and investigate what activity might have been erased.

description: A monitored log file's content hash changed while its size stayed the same or grew — possible log line injection or reordering
recommendation: Diff the current log content against the last known-good baseline where possible, look for inserted or reordered entries, and verify the log-writing process hasn't been tampered with.

description: A file inside the configured honeypot/decoy directory was modified, which should never legitimately happen since no real process accesses that path
recommendation: Any activity in a honeypot directory is inherently suspicious since it has no legitimate purpose — investigate the responsible process/user immediately and treat this as a strong intrusion signal.

description: Multiple honeypot decoy files were read within a short window by a process not associated with any backup or monitoring task
recommendation: Identify the accessing process and user immediately; rapid sequential reads of decoy files typically indicate automated reconnaissance or an active intrusion in progress rather than accidental access.

description: A running process was found executing a binary that does not match any entry in the learned or XML-configured whitelist
recommendation: Verify whether the binary is a legitimate new tool or unauthorized software; if unauthorized, terminate the process, remove the binary, and check persistence mechanisms (cron, systemd units, startup scripts) for reinfection vectors.

description: An unknown binary was detected and automatically killed per the active kill_unknow_binary policy, then reappeared on a later scan
recommendation: A binary that reappears after being killed indicates a persistence mechanism (cron job, systemd timer, or a parent process respawning it) — locate and remove the persistence source, not just the running process.

description: uid 1001 executed 'useradd' for the first time ever according to the historical command baseline
recommendation: Confirm whether this user account creation was authorized; if not, disable the newly created account, investigate how uid 1001 gained the ability to run useradd, and review sudoers/privilege configuration.

description: A watched command that a user historically ran only rarely (below the rare-execution threshold) was executed again
recommendation: Review the specific permission change made — rare use of chmod/chown by a given account can be benign but warrants a quick check for overly permissive modes or changes to sensitive files.

description: A file's ownership/permission signature changed from its established baseline
recommendation: Unexpected permission changes on sensitive system files (especially adding execute) should be reverted immediately and investigated for how the change was made and by whom.

description: A new path appeared under a monitored directory with permissions that differ from its parent directory's ownership/mode, rather than inheriting them as a normal new file would

evidence.finding: new path created with permissions differing from parent directory

recommendation: Investigate why the path was created with unexpected permissions or ownership — this can indicate privilege escalation staging or unauthorized configuration changes. Correct the permissions or remove the path once confirmed illegitimate.
